note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment options following histological upgrade to ISUP grade group 2 prostate cancer.

This 70-year-old retired farmer presents for urological review. He has a significant medical history of coronary artery disease and chronic kidney disease, with a current eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73m2. His PSA trajectory has been concerning, rising from 1.7 ng/mL in December 2023 to 5.7 ng/mL in June 2024, and now 19.0 ng/mL. He is a married man living with his partner, with adult children visiting weekly; his son acts as his primary contact for medical matters. He is an ex-smoker (11 pack-years, quit in 2019) and consumes approximately 8 units of alcohol per week. He maintains a daily walking routine of 20 minutes. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 5. He recently attended an endocrine appointment for thyroid screening.

Per rectum, a distinct nodule is palpable, consistent with a clinical T2 stage. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs, including a blood pressure of 126/69 mmHg and a heart rate of 57 bpm.
